# pokefit

> pokefit (https://pokefit.party) is a free web tool that scales a 3D-printable figure (3MF, STL, OBJ or GLB) to the
> largest size that fits inside a printed Pokéball, cuts 1–3 magnet pockets into its underside so it snaps onto
> a steel washer glued inside the ball, checks printability, and exports a Bambu Studio-ready 3MF that keeps
> painted colours. It runs entirely in the browser (Python compiled to WebAssembly via Pyodide); files are not
> uploaded. A local Python version adds Bambu Studio slicing for print time and filament use.

## What it does

- Fit: largest scale at which the figure fits the ball's inner sphere, the connector rings near the equator and
  the ring opening it must pass through when the ball closes, with a chosen clearance (default 1 mm). The figure
  stands on the steel washer, which sits in a seat at the bottom of the ball.
- Ball size: the 60 % or 100 % print of the MakerWorld model "functional Pokéball – no glue" (#2045372), or any
  inner diameter in millimetres (the ring profile scales with it).
- Magnets: 1, 2 or 3 pockets (default Ø4.18 × 2.2 mm, for 4 × 2 mm disc magnets) placed automatically to spread
  out over the washer's steel ring; draggable by hand. By default every pocket opens on the washer, so the magnet
  touches the steel; under a part that floats above the bed the magnet shows below it (at least 0.5 mm of the
  pocket must be in the figure). A "raised" option moves pockets up into such parts instead (hidden magnet, weaker
  hold), up to 2 mm above the washer. Nothing goes below the plane the figure stands on.
- Shape for the ball (on by default): the ball's floor is flat only over the washer (18 mm for M6); beyond it the
  sphere rises. Legs or a tail lying flat out past the washer are lifted along the sphere's curve (eased in, the
  lowest 30 % of the figure's height lifted fully, fading above, so arms and head are untouched). Automatic
  strength comes from the share of the low footprint beyond the washer that is a limb (free space above it, not a
  solid column) and the low footprint's aspect ratio; it is kept only if the figure then fits ≥ 1 % larger. The
  base over the washer is made flat: bumps pressed down by up to 1.2 mm, then gaps up to 2.5 mm between the
  underside and the washer filled by a separate solid "flat base" part (main colour). Only vertices move, so paint
  and texture colour are kept. Settings: bend Auto/Off/Slight/Medium/Follow the sphere, flat base diameter
  (default the washer's), press depth, fill height.
- GLB / glTF (single file): every mesh node is baked in and Y-up metres become Z-up mm (a scene over 10 units is
  kept as mm). Its colour (a texture, including the emissive slot some AI generators use; vertex colours; or flat
  materials) is sampled on sub-triangles laid out as Bambu's paint brush splits them, clustered into a few filament
  colours (shading ignored, automatic count up to 8, or a chosen 1–16), cleared of specks, and written as split
  Bambu paint on one solid part, so it slices multi-colour with crisp edges. Fewer filaments = less purge waste.
- Colorize: paint single-colour models by tapping the 3D view. A tap fills a part found from the geometry (spread
  until a concave valley sharper than an angle, default 15°, where ears, tails, legs or eyes meet the body), any
  crease (like Bambu's smart fill), a separate shell, or a brush disc. Colours can be added or changed; the result
  is written as Bambu per-triangle paint (paint_color), so it slices as multi-colour.
- Washers: catalogue of steel washers (DIN 9021 M5/M6/M8, US #10 × 3/4", US 1/4" × 1" fender) or a custom size;
  a comparison table shows the largest figure each allows with the magnets on steel. Stainless steel is not magnetic.
- Orientation: rotate about X, Y and Z by any angle; the lowest point lands on the bed.
- Checks: closed surface, normals, degenerate faces, separate shells, wall thickness (warn < 0.8 mm, fail when
  more than 5 % is < 0.4 mm), overhangs flatter than the slicer's support angle, layers that start in mid-air,
  bed contact (brim advice), and per pocket: wall, ceiling, height above the washer, position over the steel.
- Export: the figure as a Bambu Studio 3MF (opens as a project, painted colours kept); an "import" variant whose
  filament numbers are matched by colour to the user's own Bambu project slots (for File > Import > Import
  geometry only); a JSON report; and, if the user loads their copy of the ball model, the bottom shell with a
  washer seat cut in.
- Bambu presets: besides a project 3MF, the settings button reads Bambu Studio's preset exports (File > Export >
  Export Preset Bundle: a .bbscfg printer bundle, a .bbsflmt filament bundle, or a printer/filament/process
  presets .zip). A preset is a diff over a system preset (`inherits`); the local version resolves it against the
  installed Bambu Studio's profiles, the browser lays it over the project's closest slot (marked approximate).
  Filament presets become selectable materials, process presets for the same printer a "Process" choice, a
  printer preset for the project's printer is applied, and a filament whose temperature for the project's plate
  is 0 is flagged (Bambu refuses to slice it).
- Colour-change cost: per layer, which filaments print (from the paint); per nozzle, the changes when it
  keeps its loaded filament; on a two-nozzle printer (X2D, H2D) the best split of filaments between nozzles.
  Shown as filament changes, extra time and purge grams, for the figure and for every palette size of a
  textured GLB. Calibrated on Bambu CLI slices (about 105 s and 0.4 g per change, 18 s per nozzle switch);
  exports keep Bambu's own "Auto For Flush" nozzle assignment, which matched or beat the planner.
- Handoff from other apps: `?url=<model URL>` (CORS), or open pokefit and post
  `{type: "pokefit:load", name, data: ArrayBuffer}` after it announces `pokefit:ready` (trusted origins only).
- Multi-figure 3MF files: a picker chooses which figure to fit.

## Local version

- Source: https://github.com/tribixbite/pokefit (Python 3.11+, numpy/scipy/trimesh/manifold3d/shapely; web UI in
  TypeScript with three.js, built with bun).
- `pip install -e .`, then `python -m pokefit serve --open` (web UI with Bambu Studio slicing: 1× and 10× plate
  print time, filament grams, supports verdict) or `python -m pokefit fit figure.3mf --diameter 44 --magnets 2
  --out DIR --slice`.
